facts.statement: The species Xuanhanosaurus qilixiaensis was named by Dong Zhiming in 1984.
facts.quote: The type species Xuanhanosaurus qilixiaensis was named by Dong Zhiming in 1984.

facts.statement: The fossil specimen was recovered in 1979 during a dinosaur survey in Sichuan Province.
facts.quote: The specimen was recovered in 1979, when the author was conducting a Dinosaurian Fossil survey in Sichuan Province

facts.statement: The holotype specimen IVPP V.6729 was found in the Lower Shaximiao Formation in China.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen, IVPP V.6729, was found in China's Lower Shaximiao Formation.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of a partial skeleton lacking a skull, including a scapula, coracoid, possible sternum, forelimb bones, and some dorsal vertebrae.
facts.quote: It consists of a partial skeleton without a skull, namely a scapula missing the posterior end, coracoid, a possible sternum, humerus, radius, ulna, manus, as well a few fragmentary dorsal vertebrae.

facts.statement: Xuanhanosaurus lived in the Sichuan Basin, China, during the Middle Jurassic (Bathonian) approximately 166 million years ago.
facts.quote: Xuanhanosaurus (meaning "Xuanhan lizard") is a genus of theropod dinosaur that lived during the Middle Jurassic (Bathonian) of the Sichuan Basin, China, around 166 million years ago.

facts.statement: Xuanhanosaurus lived in what is now Asia during the Middle Jurassic Callovian stage, between 167 and 161 million years ago.
facts.quote: Xuanhanosaurus qilixiaensis es la única especie conocida del género extinto Xuanhanosaurus ("lagarto de Xuanhan"), un dinosaurio terópodo tetanuro, que vivió a mediados del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente entre 167 y 161 millones de años, en el Calloviense, en lo que es hoy Asia.

facts.statement: Xuanhanosaurus was approximately 4.8 meters long and weighed 265 kilograms.
facts.quote: Xuanhanosaurus, originally thought to be around 6 m long, was approximately 4.8 meters (16 ft) in length, with a weight of 265 kilograms (585 lb).

facts.statement: Xuanhanosaurus measured approximately 4.5 meters in length and weighed 250 kilograms.
facts.quote: Xuanhanosaurus medía aproximadamente 4,5 metros de largo, con un peso de 250 kilogramos.

facts.statement: Xuanhanosaurus is characterized by having strong, long forelimbs that were over 65 centimeters long, a size usually reduced in other dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Xuanhanosaurus se caracteriza por poseer brazos fuertes y largos, de más de 65 centímetros de largo, que normalmente se encuentran reducidos.

facts.statement: The hand retains four metacarpals, and the scapula has a distinct acromial prominence unlike the flattened glenoid region seen in other theropods.
facts.quote: El brazo es robusto, y la mano conserva cuatro metacarpianos, mientras que el omóplato tiene una prominencia acromial absolutamente distinta de la forma aplanada de la región glenoidea en otros terópodos.

facts.statement: Most studies agree that Xuanhanosaurus is a tetanuran, possibly a basal allosauroid, notable for retaining a vestigial fourth metacarpal.
facts.quote: Although it has been known for more than 40 years, this taxon has been the subject of very few studies, although most seem to agree that it is a tetanuran, possibly a basal allosauroid, highlighting the fact that it has a vestigial fourth metacarpal.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Xuanhanosaurus walked on four legs; while the describer suggested it was the only known four-legged meat-eater, later paleontologists argue it walked on hind legs because arm pronation was impossible.
facts.quote: If so, it would be the only known four-legged meat-eater among dinosaurs. Later paleontologists have not agreed with Dong's original assessment. They think this dinosaur walked on its hind legs as other theropods did, pronation of the lower arm being impossible.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest the strong arms of Xuanhanosaurus may have been used for catching prey.
facts.quote: The strong arms could instead have been useful in catching prey.

facts.statement: Recent work indicates Xuanhanosaurus retains ceratosaurian-like short phalanges similar to those found in Saltriovenator.
facts.quote: Some recent work have notified that beyond the 4th metarcarpal, Xuanhanosaurus also retains ceratosaurian-like short phalanges II-1, similar in length to the ones recovered on Saltriovenator.

facts.statement: Dong originally assigned Xuanhanosaurus to Megalosauridae and considered it a middle-stage tetanuran due to its vestigial fourth metacarpal.
facts.quote: Originally, Xuanhanosaurus was assigned by Dong to the Megalosauridae, when this group was meant to include a larger amount of taxa, and was argued to be in the middle stage of the evolution of the Tetanurae due to its vestigial fourth metacarpals.

facts.statement: In 2009, Roger Benson found Xuanhanosaurus belonged to a primitive lineage of Megalosauroidea.
facts.quote: Latter it was found by Roger Benson in 2009 to belong to a primitive lineage of the Megalosauroidea.

facts.statement: In 2018, it was argued that Xuanhanosaurus belongs to early-diverging branches of the ceratosaurian-tetanuran node based on features like the vestigial fourth metacarpal.
facts.quote: In 2018, based on several conditions such as the length and retention of the vestigial 4th metacarpal, it was argued that this taxon and "Szechuanosaurus" zigongensis belong to early-diverging branches of the ceratosaurian-tetanuran node.

facts.statement: In 2019, Rauhut and Pol placed Xuanhanosaurus outside Metriacanthosauridae as the basalmost member of Allosauroidea.
facts.quote: In 2019, Rauhut and Pol recovered Xuanhanosaurus outside of Metriacanthosauridae, as the basalmost member of Allosauroidea.

facts.statement: Dong assigned Xuanhanosaurus to Megalosauridae, while others like Holtz et al. consider it a non-coelurosaurian tetanuran.
facts.quote: Fue asignado por Dong a la familia Megalosauridae, Roger Benson consideró en 2009 que Xuanhanosaurus pertenecía a un linaje primitivo de Megalosauroidea. Otros como Holtz et al. lo consideran un tetanuro no celurosauriano.

facts.statement: A 2010 study by Benson and colleagues found it was more likely that Xuanhanosaurus was the most primitive known member of the Metriacanthosauridae family.
facts.quote: Un estudio más reciente realizado por Benson y sus colegas en 2010 encontró que era más probable que fuera el miembro conocido más primitivo de la familia Metriacanthosauridae.

facts.statement: In 2019, Rauhut and Pol recovered Xuanhanosaurus outside Metriacanthosauridae as the most basal member of Allosauroidea.
facts.quote: En 2019, Rauhut y Pol recuperaron a Xuanhanosaurus fuera de Metriacanthosauridae, como el miembro más basal de Allosauroidea.

facts.statement: The Paleobiology Database lists the parent group of Xuanhanosaurus as Piatnitzkysauridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Piatnitzkysauridae

facts.statement: The Paleobiology Database lists the family of Xuanhanosaurus as Piatnitzkysauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Piatnitzkysauridae

rejected.statement: While the fourth metacarpal is a notable feature, some argue that a specific carpal shape represents a second stage in the evolution of the semilunate carpal.
rejected.quote: The retention of the 4th metarcarpal is the most notorious feature of this taxon, yet the presence of a convex proximal surface on the distal carpal 2 has been used to argue it represents a second stage in the evolution of the "semilunate" carpal.

rejected.statement: A 2010 study by Benson and colleagues suggested Xuanhanosaurus was likely the most primitive known member of the Metriacanthosauridae family.
rejected.quote: A more recent study by Benson and colleagues in 2010 found that it was more likely to be the most primitive known member of the Metriacanthosauridae family.
